title_guess: WPI: how wholesale price inflation is measured in India

segments.teaches: inflation is a rise in prices of goods and services over time

elements.what: grocery bag (goods) & delivery scooter (services)
price vs year axes with rising dotted line and curved inflation arrow
like-count progress bar with 'target' tooltip (engagement prompt)

segments.notes: same intro composition as E15 (asset reuse across videos)

segments.teaches: inflation is measured by WPI and CPI; a grandparent's memory of 1000 vs today's 5000 shows why we compare prices over time

elements.what: INFLATION heading
INFLATION -> WPI and CPI with full names
store, shopper with basket, family on sofa with TV, elder in armchair
small ? above the family
speech bubbles: '5000 Rs' over the shopper and the elder remembering 1000
first row: basket | price in our time 1000 | current price 5000

segments.notes: story hook with black silhouette icons; running example 1000 -> 5000

segments.teaches: a price index compares the current price of a fixed basket with a base-year price: 1000 to 5000 is a 400% rise; base year is 2011-12

elements.what: blue one-row table: basket | price in our time | current price | % increase 400%
basket definition hanging from the basket icon
column header 'price in our time' struck, 'base year (2011-12)' written above

segments.notes: strike-and-replace used on a label (everyday word -> technical term), not on a number

segments.teaches: the supply chain producer -> wholesaler -> retailer -> consumer has three price points, measured by PPI, WPI and CPI

elements.what: WPI gets a cart of boxes, CPI a grocery bag; key words highlighted
factory -> warehouse -> store -> person, with pink, blue and cream coloured bands on the arrows
producer price / wholesale price / consumer price labels
light-blue strip 'measure average price level' holding PPI, WPI, CPI with down arrows
prices 10, 15 rupees written in the bands

segments.notes: basket icon slides away first; colour band on each arrow is reused as the column colour of its index

segments.teaches: prices rise at each stage (10, 15, 20); PPI is common worldwide while India uses WPI and CPI; WPI looks only at the first bulk sale

elements.what: third price 20 rupees in the consumer band
green up arrows over each of the three prices
blue tick badge on PPI
small India silhouettes on WPI and CPI
note under WPI about first point of bulk sale

segments.notes: map silhouette used as a 'used in India' badge next to an index name

segments.teaches: WPI is used for macro-level policy making

elements.what: green 'macro-level policy making' chip under the WPI note

segments.notes: supply-chain part cleared, only the top tree and the WPI note stay

segments.teaches: the WPI basket has 697 commodities in three groups (fuel and power, manufactured, primary) with weights 13.15%, 64.23%, 22.62%

elements.what: blue 'WPI - wholesale price index' heading chip top-left (stays for the rest of the video)
cart of boxes labelled BASKET, 697 commodities
basket -> fuel & power / manufactured products / primary articles
boxed example lists beside each group
coloured highlighter on sub-group words with matching-colour example lines
weight percentages written on each branch

segments.notes: colour-matched highlighting: a highlighted word and its example bullet share the same colour

segments.teaches: each group is split into items with their own weights

elements.what: coloured group headers with weights (yellow, pink, purple)
small fuel table, long manufactured-products table (~22 rows), primary-articles table
weight columns filled light blue

segments.notes: dense real data tables; header colours match the earlier tree

segments.teaches: for one item (a chair) many price quotations are collected, with base and current prices that exclude indirect taxes

elements.what: realistic render of an armchair as the sample item
quotation no. 1-11 column, then base price and current price columns appear
note box: total number of quotations used
bracket under the price columns with a note about indirect taxes

segments.notes: background switches to light grey; table grows column by column

segments.teaches: each quote's price relative = current/base x 100; their geometric mean gives the item's elementary index (193.77) using the Jevons formula

elements.what: price relative column added
(current price / base price) x 100 with curved arrow to the column header
price relative column filled blue with a bracket bar
arrow from column to '(geometric mean)'
elementary price index box with red 193.77
yellow strip naming the Jevons index formula

segments.notes: worked calculation with real-looking numbers inside a table

segments.teaches: each item's index I is multiplied by its weight W; summing I x W over all items and dividing by total weight gives WPI

elements.what: weight tables return; furniture row highlighted yellow and its weight cell boxed
armchair render at bottom-left with elementary index 193.77 callout
line from chair index (I1) to the boxed weight (W1)
sum (I x W) / sum W, with basket cart icon

segments.notes: links the micro example (one chair) back to the macro table by a single connector line

segments.teaches: WPI formula: Jevons for item indices, Laspeyres for the weighted total; WPI measures the change month by month against base year 2011-12 = 100

elements.what: WPI = sum (I x W) / sum W
orange Jevons and Laspeyres labels pointing at parts of the formula
green note: WPI measures monthly change
rainbow strip of months April to March
base year row of 100 under each month

segments.notes: white background again; formula annotated with labelled pointer arrows

segments.teaches: WPI is point-to-point: each month this year is compared with the same month of the base year

elements.what: second row 2022-23 values (114, 115, 113 ... 105, blanks for future months)
down arrows from each base value to its month's value
August column boxed in blue
point-to-point explanation line

segments.notes: table with one highlighted column to show the comparison rule

segments.teaches: a year of monthly WPI values plotted as a trend

elements.what: line chart with dots and light-blue shaded area, monthly WPI rising then falling
channel app phone mock-up and store badges over the chart

segments.notes: mid-video promo overlay covers part of the chart

segments.teaches: WPI is published by DPIIT under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (earlier called DIPP)

elements.what: national emblem on a ministry name card
megaphone announcing WPI
plug-and-cable connector from the department card to the megaphone
dark chips with department names and an old-name chip with up arrow
